constraints.action: Stage AKI severity using KDIGO criteria (Stage 1, 2, or 3)
Monitor serum creatinine and urine output to detect AKI early
Obtain baseline creatinine measurement
Assess AKI risk factors including nephrotoxic medications, contrast exposure, sepsis, and hypovolemia
Discontinue all nephrotoxic agents when possible in patients with or at risk for AKI
Hold ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs in patients with developing AKI
Maintain euvolemia in patients with AKI using isotonic crystalloids
Avoid fluid overload
Monitor fluid balance closely
Assess hydration status regularly
Perform diagnostic workup for AKI etiology: urinalysis, urine electrolytes (FENa), renal ultrasound to evaluate for obstruction, serum electrolytes (BMP), complete blood count (CBC), and blood gas
Consult nephrology early for AKI Stage 2 or higher, or when etiology is unclear, or when renal replacement therapy may be needed
Order serial creatinine monitoring (every 6-12 hours for Stage 2-3)

Initiate renal replacement therapy (RRT) emergently when life-threatening changes exist: refractory hyperkalemia, severe metabolic acidosis, pulmonary edema refractory to diuretics, or uremic complications
Monitor potassium closely in AKI patients
Treat hyperkalemia with calcium gluconate for cardiac stabilization, insulin/glucose for potassium shifting, and sodium bicarbonate if acidotic
Monitor ECG for hyperkalemia signs
Check baseline eGFR before contrast exposure
Use the lowest possible contrast volume
Provide IV isotonic saline hydration before and after contrast exposure for high-risk patients (eGFR < 30)
Pre-hydration: 1-1.5 mL/kg/hr for 6-12 hours before procedure
Post-hydration: continue for 6-12 hours after
Use low-osmolar or iso-osmolar contrast media in patients at risk for CA-AKI
Avoid high-osmolar contrast
Minimize contrast volume
Hold metformin before contrast procedures in patients with eGFR < 30
Monitor serum creatinine at 48-72 hours after contrast exposure
Resume medications when renal function is stable
Avoid additional nephrotoxic exposures in the peri-procedural period
